subject: Ancient History
statement: The script of the Indus Valley Civilisation has never been deciphered.
explanation: Fact. Despite thousands of recovered seals, the Indus script remains undeciphered, unlike Brahmi or Kharosthi.

subject: Ancient History
statement: Ashoka's edicts were written primarily in Sanskrit using the Devanagari script.
explanation: Bluff. Most edicts were composed in Prakrit and written in Brahmi script, with Kharosthi in the northwest.

subject: Ancient History
statement: The Rigveda is the oldest of the four Vedas.
explanation: Fact. The Rigveda is the earliest Veda, followed by the Sama, Yajur and Atharva Vedas.

subject: Ancient History
statement: Chandragupta Maurya was the founder of the Gupta Empire.
explanation: Bluff. Chandragupta Maurya founded the Maurya Empire; the Gupta line was founded by Sri Gupta centuries later.

subject: Ancient History
statement: The Greek ambassador Megasthenes wrote the Indica at the court of Chandragupta Maurya.
explanation: Fact. Megasthenes was Seleucus Nicator's envoy to Chandragupta Maurya and recorded his observations in the Indica.

subject: Ancient History
statement: The Harappan port site of Lothal is located in present-day Rajasthan.
explanation: Bluff. Lothal, with its famous dockyard, lies in Gujarat; Kalibangan is the well-known Harappan site in Rajasthan.

subject: Ancient History
statement: The Third Buddhist Council was held at Pataliputra under Ashoka's patronage.
explanation: Fact. The Third Council met at Pataliputra around 250 BCE under Ashoka, presided over by Moggaliputta Tissa.

subject: Ancient History
statement: The Arthashastra was written by Banabhatta.
explanation: Bluff. The Arthashastra is attributed to Kautilya (Chanakya); Banabhatta wrote the Harshacharita.

subject: Ancient History
statement: Xuanzang's 7th-century account describes Nalanda in a state of ruin.
explanation: Bluff. Xuanzang saw Nalanda at its peak; its ruined state was recorded much later, by Dharmasvamin in the 13th century.

subject: Ancient History
statement: The Junagadh inscription of Rudradaman is the earliest long inscription in chaste Sanskrit.
explanation: Fact. The 2nd-century CE Junagadh rock inscription of the Saka ruler Rudradaman I is the first major inscription in pure Sanskrit.

subject: Ancient History
statement: The iron pillar at Mehrauli was erected by Ashoka.
explanation: Bluff. The rust-resistant pillar names a king 'Chandra', widely identified as Gupta ruler Chandragupta II, not Ashoka.

subject: Ancient History
statement: Sangam-era Tamil texts refer to Roman and Greek traders as Yavanas.
explanation: Fact. Sangam literature uses 'Yavana' for Westerners, reflecting the thriving Indo-Roman trade in ports like Muziris.

subject: Medieval History
statement: The Vijayanagara Empire was founded by the brothers Harihara and Bukka in the 14th century.
explanation: Fact. Harihara I and Bukka I founded Vijayanagara around 1336 CE on the banks of the Tungabhadra.

subject: Medieval History
statement: The First Battle of Panipat in 1526 was fought between Babur and Sher Shah Suri.
explanation: Bluff. Babur defeated Ibrahim Lodi at Panipat in 1526; Sher Shah rose against Babur's son Humayun later.

subject: Medieval History
statement: Qutb-ud-din Aibak was the first Sultan of the Delhi Sultanate.
explanation: Fact. Aibak founded the Slave (Mamluk) dynasty in 1206, beginning the Delhi Sultanate.

subject: Medieval History
statement: Akbar built the Taj Mahal in memory of his wife.
explanation: Bluff. The Taj Mahal was built by Shah Jahan in memory of Mumtaz Mahal, not by Akbar.

subject: Medieval History
statement: Alauddin Khalji introduced strict market price controls in Delhi.
explanation: Fact. Alauddin fixed prices of grain and essentials and set up regulated markets to sustain his large army cheaply.

subject: Medieval History
statement: The Moroccan traveller Ibn Battuta visited India during the reign of Akbar.
explanation: Bluff. Ibn Battuta came in the 14th century under Muhammad bin Tughlaq, who made him qazi of Delhi.

subject: Medieval History
statement: Muhammad bin Tughlaq shifted his capital from Delhi to Daulatabad.
explanation: Fact. He moved the capital to Daulatabad (Devagiri) around 1327, an experiment he later reversed.

subject: Medieval History
statement: The Battle of Talikota in 1565 led to the destruction of the Bahmani kingdom.
explanation: Bluff. Talikota shattered the Vijayanagara Empire; the victors were the Deccan Sultanates that had emerged from the Bahmani kingdom.

subject: Medieval History
statement: Krishnadevaraya authored the Telugu work Amuktamalyada.
explanation: Fact. The Vijayanagara ruler Krishnadevaraya wrote Amuktamalyada, a Telugu classic on the saint Andal.

subject: Medieval History
statement: The Qutub Minar was completed by Qutb-ud-din Aibak.
explanation: Bluff. Aibak only began the minar; it was completed by his successor Iltutmish and later repaired by Firoz Shah Tughlaq.

subject: Medieval History
statement: Rajendra Chola I built a new capital at Gangaikonda Cholapuram after his Ganga expedition.
explanation: Fact. Rajendra I took the title Gangaikonda after his northern campaign and founded Gangaikonda Cholapuram as his capital.

subject: Medieval History
statement: Malik Kafur led Alauddin Khalji's military campaigns into Bengal.
explanation: Bluff. Malik Kafur's famous campaigns were into the Deccan and south — Devagiri, Warangal, Dwarasamudra and Madurai — not Bengal.

subject: Modern History
statement: The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885 by Bal Gangadhar Tilak.
explanation: Bluff. The Congress was founded in 1885 by Allan Octavian Hume, a retired British civil servant; Tilak joined later.

subject: Modern History
statement: The Revolt of 1857 began with the sepoys at Meerut.
explanation: Fact. The uprising broke out at Meerut on 10 May 1857 before the sepoys marched to Delhi.

subject: Modern History
statement: Mahatma Gandhi launched the Dandi March in 1930 against the salt tax.
explanation: Fact. Gandhi marched from Sabarmati to Dandi in March–April 1930, breaking the salt law to launch Civil Disobedience.

subject: Modern History
statement: The Quit India Movement was launched in 1922.
explanation: Bluff. Quit India was launched in August 1942; 1922 was when Gandhi withdrew Non-Cooperation after Chauri Chaura.

subject: Modern History
statement: The Partition of Bengal in 1905 was carried out by Lord Curzon.
explanation: Fact. Curzon partitioned Bengal in 1905, triggering the Swadeshi Movement; the partition was annulled in 1911.

subject: Modern History
statement: The Simon Commission was boycotted because it included no British members.
explanation: Bluff. It was an all-British commission; Indians boycotted it precisely because it had no Indian member.

subject: Modern History
statement: The Swaraj Party was founded by C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru.
explanation: Fact. Das and Motilal Nehru formed the Swaraj Party in 1923 to contest council elections after Non-Cooperation ended.

subject: Modern History
statement: The Poona Pact of 1932 was signed between Gandhi and Jinnah.
explanation: Bluff. The Poona Pact was between Gandhi and B.R. Ambedkar, replacing separate electorates for Depressed Classes with reserved seats.

subject: Modern History
statement: The Ghadar Party was founded in 1913 in San Francisco.
explanation: Fact. Indian emigrants on the US Pacific coast, led by figures like Lala Har Dayal, founded the Ghadar Party in 1913.

subject: Modern History
statement: The Indian National Army was originally founded by Subhas Chandra Bose.
explanation: Bluff. The INA was first raised in 1942 under Mohan Singh; Bose revived and led it from 1943.

subject: Modern History
statement: Lord Dalhousie annexed Awadh in 1856 on grounds of misgovernance, not the Doctrine of Lapse.
explanation: Fact. Awadh had heirs, so Lapse did not apply; it was annexed citing maladministration by Nawab Wajid Ali Shah.

subject: Modern History
statement: The Lucknow Pact of 1916 was an agreement between the Congress and the British government.
explanation: Bluff. The Lucknow Pact was between the Congress and the Muslim League, in which Congress accepted separate electorates.

subject: Art and Culture
statement: Bharatanatyam is a classical dance form of Tamil Nadu.
explanation: Fact. Bharatanatyam evolved in Tamil Nadu's temples and is among India's oldest recognised classical dances.

subject: Art and Culture
statement: Kathakali is a classical dance form of Odisha.
explanation: Bluff. Kathakali belongs to Kerala; Odisha's classical dance is Odissi.

subject: Art and Culture
statement: The Sun Temple at Konark is located in Odisha.
explanation: Fact. The 13th-century Konark Sun Temple, built by Narasimhadeva I, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site in Odisha.

subject: Art and Culture
statement: The Ajanta caves are famous mainly for their Jain sculptures.
explanation: Bluff. Ajanta is renowned for Buddhist murals and rock-cut monasteries, not Jain art.

subject: Art and Culture
statement: Sattriya, the classical dance of Assam, was introduced by the Vaishnavite saint Sankaradeva.
explanation: Fact. Sattriya originated in the Vaishnavite monasteries (sattras) established by Srimanta Sankaradeva in the 15th–16th century.

subject: Art and Culture
statement: Hindustani vocalist Bhimsen Joshi belonged to the Gwalior gharana.
explanation: Bluff. Bhimsen Joshi, a Bharat Ratna awardee, was the towering voice of the Kirana gharana.

subject: Art and Culture
statement: The Khajuraho temples were built by the Chandela dynasty.
explanation: Fact. The Chandelas built the Khajuraho temple complex in Madhya Pradesh between the 10th and 12th centuries.

subject: Art and Culture
statement: Madhubani painting is a traditional folk art of West Bengal.
explanation: Bluff. Madhubani (Mithila) painting comes from Bihar; West Bengal is known for Kalighat and Patachitra scroll painting.

subject: Art and Culture
statement: The Chola bronze Nataraja depicts Shiva performing the Ananda Tandava.
explanation: Fact. The iconic Chola Nataraja shows Shiva in the Ananda Tandava, the cosmic dance of bliss, within a ring of fire.

subject: Art and Culture
statement: The Gandhara school of art primarily used white marble.
explanation: Bluff. Gandhara sculptors mainly used grey-blue schist and stucco; the Mathura school used spotted red sandstone.

subject: Art and Culture
statement: Sankirtana, the ritual singing of Manipur, is on UNESCO's Intangible Cultural Heritage list.
explanation: Fact. Manipuri Sankirtana, performed in temples and homes of Vaishnava communities, was inscribed by UNESCO in 2013.

subject: Art and Culture
statement: The Kailasa temple at Ellora was excavated under the patronage of the Cholas.
explanation: Bluff. The monolithic Kailasa temple was carved under Rashtrakuta king Krishna I in the 8th century.

subject: Geography
statement: The Ganga is the longest river flowing within India.
explanation: Fact. The Ganga, at over 2,500 km, is the longest river within India's territory.

subject: Geography
statement: The Thar Desert is located mainly in Gujarat.
explanation: Bluff. The Thar lies mainly in Rajasthan, with smaller extensions into Gujarat, Punjab and Haryana.

subject: Geography
statement: India's southernmost point, Indira Point, lies in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands.
explanation: Fact. Indira Point sits at the southern tip of Great Nicobar Island, south of Kanyakumari on the mainland.

subject: Geography
statement: The Sundarbans delta is formed by the Godavari river.
explanation: Bluff. The Sundarbans is part of the Ganga–Brahmaputra delta, the largest delta in the world.

subject: Geography
statement: The Tropic of Cancer passes through only two Indian states.
explanation: Bluff. It passes through eight states: Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Jharkhand, West Bengal, Tripura and Mizoram.

subject: Geography
statement: The Narmada flows westward through a rift valley into the Arabian Sea.
explanation: Fact. The Narmada flows west between the Vindhya and Satpura ranges through a rift valley, forming an estuary, not a delta.

subject: Geography
statement: Kanchenjunga is the highest peak located entirely within India.
explanation: Bluff. Kanchenjunga straddles the India–Nepal border; Nanda Devi is the highest peak entirely within India.

subject: Geography
statement: Loktak Lake, famous for its floating phumdis, is located in Manipur.
explanation: Fact. Loktak in Manipur is the largest freshwater lake in northeast India, known for its floating vegetation islands.

subject: Geography
statement: The Ten Degree Channel separates the Andaman Islands from the Nicobar Islands.
explanation: Fact. The Ten Degree Channel, lying roughly along 10°N latitude, divides the Andamans from the Nicobars.

subject: Geography
statement: The Duncan Passage separates Little Andaman from Car Nicobar.
explanation: Bluff. The Duncan Passage lies between South Andaman and Little Andaman; the Ten Degree Channel separates Little Andaman from Car Nicobar.

subject: Geography
statement: The Godavari has the largest drainage basin among peninsular rivers.
explanation: Fact. The Godavari, called the Dakshina Ganga, has India's second-largest basin after the Ganga and the largest in the peninsula.

subject: Geography
statement: The Nine Degree Channel separates Minicoy from the Maldives.
explanation: Bluff. The Eight Degree Channel separates Minicoy from the Maldives; the Nine Degree Channel separates Minicoy from the rest of Lakshadweep.

subject: Economy
statement: India's GST applies a single unified tax rate to every good and service.
explanation: Bluff. GST has multiple slabs, and items like petroleum and alcohol for human consumption remain outside it.

subject: Economy
statement: The Reserve Bank of India is the sole issuer of India's currency notes.
explanation: Fact. The RBI issues all currency notes; the government mints coins and issues the one-rupee note.

subject: Economy
statement: Repo rate is the rate at which banks lend money to the RBI.
explanation: Bluff. Repo is the rate at which the RBI lends to banks; banks parking funds with the RBI earn the reverse repo rate.

subject: Economy
statement: GDP measures the total value of goods and services produced within a country.
explanation: Fact. Gross Domestic Product counts final goods and services produced within a country's borders in a given period.

subject: Economy
statement: The RBI's Monetary Policy Committee has six members.
explanation: Fact. The MPC has three RBI members, including the Governor, and three members appointed by the central government.

subject: Economy
statement: NITI Aayog was created in 2015 to replace the Finance Commission.
explanation: Bluff. NITI Aayog replaced the Planning Commission; the Finance Commission is a constitutional body that still exists.

subject: Economy
statement: India's inflation-targeting framework sets a CPI target of 4% with a tolerance band of 2%.
explanation: Fact. Under the amended RBI Act, the target is 4% CPI inflation with a band of plus or minus 2%.

subject: Economy
statement: Fiscal deficit refers to the gap between a country's exports and imports.
explanation: Bluff. That gap is the trade deficit; fiscal deficit is government expenditure exceeding receipts, excluding borrowings.

subject: Economy
statement: The Marginal Standing Facility lets banks borrow overnight from the RBI at a rate above the repo rate.
explanation: Fact. MSF is an emergency overnight window priced above the repo rate, forming the ceiling of the policy corridor.

subject: Economy
statement: Open Market Operations involve the RBI buying and selling corporate bonds.
explanation: Bluff. OMOs involve the purchase and sale of government securities to manage liquidity, not corporate bonds.

subject: Economy
statement: In the Union Budget, disinvestment proceeds are classified as capital receipts.
explanation: Fact. Sale of government equity is a non-debt capital receipt, since it reduces the government's assets.

subject: Economy
statement: India's Wholesale Price Index includes the prices of services.
explanation: Bluff. The WPI covers only goods; services are captured in the Consumer Price Index.

subject: Environment
statement: The Chipko Movement of the 1970s saw villagers hug trees to stop deforestation.
explanation: Fact. Villagers in the Himalayan region, many of them women like Gaura Devi, hugged trees to resist commercial logging.

subject: Environment
statement: Project Tiger was launched in the 1990s.
explanation: Bluff. Project Tiger was launched in 1973 with nine reserves, starting with Jim Corbett National Park.

subject: Environment
statement: The ozone layer protects the Earth from harmful ultraviolet radiation.
explanation: Fact. Stratospheric ozone absorbs most of the Sun's harmful UV-B radiation before it reaches the surface.

subject: Environment
statement: The Sundarbans are famous as the habitat of the Asiatic lion.
explanation: Bluff. The Sundarbans are home to the Royal Bengal tiger; Asiatic lions survive only in Gujarat's Gir forest.

subject: Environment
statement: The Ramsar Convention deals with the conservation of wetlands.
explanation: Fact. The 1971 Ramsar Convention promotes wise use of wetlands, and India has dozens of designated Ramsar sites.

subject: Environment
statement: The Montreal Protocol addresses climate change caused by greenhouse gases.
explanation: Bluff. The Montreal Protocol phases out ozone-depleting substances; greenhouse gases are covered by the Kyoto Protocol and Paris Agreement.

subject: Environment
statement: Keibul Lamjao, the world's only floating national park, is home to the sangai deer.
explanation: Fact. Keibul Lamjao on Loktak Lake in Manipur shelters the endangered sangai, or brow-antlered deer.

subject: Environment
statement: The Great Indian Bustard is found mainly in the forests of Kerala.
explanation: Bluff. The critically endangered bustard inhabits dry grasslands, chiefly in Rajasthan and Gujarat.

subject: Environment
statement: Eco-Sensitive Zones around protected areas are notified under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
explanation: Fact. ESZs are declared by the central government under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986 as buffers around parks and sanctuaries.

subject: Environment
statement: The National Green Tribunal was established under the Environment (Protection) Act, 1986.
explanation: Bluff. The NGT was created by its own statute, the National Green Tribunal Act of 2010.

subject: Environment
statement: The dugong, India's only herbivorous marine mammal, is found in the Gulf of Mannar.
explanation: Fact. Dugongs graze on seagrass beds in the Gulf of Mannar, Palk Bay, Gulf of Kutch and the Andamans.

subject: Environment
statement: Blue carbon refers to carbon captured by terrestrial forests.
explanation: Bluff. Blue carbon is carbon stored by coastal and marine ecosystems such as mangroves, seagrasses and salt marshes.

subject: Polity
statement: Dr. B.R. Ambedkar chaired the Drafting Committee of the Constitution.
explanation: Fact. Ambedkar headed the seven-member Drafting Committee set up by the Constituent Assembly in 1947.

subject: Polity
statement: The President of India is directly elected by the people.
explanation: Bluff. The President is elected indirectly by an electoral college of MPs and elected MLAs.

subject: Polity
statement: Fundamental Duties were not part of the original Constitution and were added later by an amendment.
explanation: Fact. Fundamental Duties (Article 51A) were inserted by the 42nd Amendment in 1976, on the Swaran Singh Committee's recommendation.

subject: Polity
statement: The Rajya Sabha can be dissolved by the President.
explanation: Bluff. The Rajya Sabha is a permanent body; a third of its members retire every two years, but it is never dissolved.

subject: Polity
statement: India's Election Commission currently functions as a multi-member body, not headed solely by the Chief Election Commissioner.
explanation: Fact. The Commission comprises the Chief Election Commissioner and two Election Commissioners with equal decision-making power.

subject: Polity
statement: A Money Bill can be introduced in either House of Parliament.
explanation: Bluff. A Money Bill can be introduced only in the Lok Sabha, and only on the President's recommendation.

subject: Polity
statement: The Directive Principles of State Policy were borrowed from the Irish Constitution.
explanation: Fact. The DPSP concept came from Ireland, which had itself adapted it from the Spanish Constitution.

subject: Polity
statement: The 73rd Constitutional Amendment gave constitutional status to urban local bodies.
explanation: Bluff. The 73rd Amendment covered rural panchayats; urban local bodies got constitutional status through the 74th Amendment.

subject: Polity
statement: The Ninth Schedule was added by the very first Constitutional Amendment in 1951.
explanation: Fact. The First Amendment of 1951 created the Ninth Schedule to shield land-reform laws from judicial review.

subject: Polity
statement: The Vice-President can be removed only through impeachment for violating the Constitution.
explanation: Bluff. Impeachment applies to the President; the Vice-President is removed by a Rajya Sabha resolution agreed to by the Lok Sabha, with no grounds specified.

subject: Polity
statement: The Speaker's decision on whether a bill is a Money Bill is final.
explanation: Fact. Article 110(3) makes the Lok Sabha Speaker's certification of a Money Bill final.

subject: Polity
statement: The Attorney General of India holds office for a fixed six-year term.
explanation: Bluff. The Attorney General has no fixed term and holds office during the pleasure of the President.
